explanation: Coal, iron and water-powered cotton mills led the way. James Watt's improved steam engine, patented in 1769, later let factories be built far from fast rivers.

claims.text: The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain in the second half of the 1700s.
France, Germany and the United States industrialized later than Great Britain.
Early British industry relied on coal, iron and water-powered cotton mills.
James Watt patented his improved steam engine, with a separate condenser, in 1769.
Steam power allowed factories to be built away from rivers.
